setting: A student reports a lost campus ID at the Campus Card Office and learns how to get a replacement.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a staff member at the campus card office.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. I think I lost my campus ID. I had it yesterday in the dining hall, but it's not in my wallet now.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Okay. First, I can deactivate the old card so nobody else can use your meal plan or building access.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Please do that. How long does a replacement take?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: If you have another photo ID with you, we can print a new card today—usually in about twenty minutes. There's a ten-dollar replacement fee.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I have my driver's license. Can I pay with a card?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes, debit or credit. Also, check the lost-and-found desk in the student union. Dining hall staff sometimes turn IDs in there within a day.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I already called them—nothing yet. I'll go ahead and replace it. I need library access tonight.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Understood. Stand on the marks for the photo, and I'll deactivate the old number now. Your new card will work as soon as it's printed.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Great. One more question—does this affect my bus pass?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: The campus shuttle is linked to your student account, not the physical card number, so that stays active. Only door access and meal swipes move to the new card.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Perfect. Thanks for walking me through it.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.A: Applying for a first-time campus meal plan
options.B: Replacing a lost campus ID card
options.C: Reporting a problem with the campus shuttle
options.D: Changing the student's dining hall schedule

questions.explanation: The student lost his ID and arranges deactivation plus a same-day replacement.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A because the meal plan is mentioned—only as a reason to deactivate the old card.

questions.narrator_text: What will the staff member do first?

options.D: Issue a temporary paper pass for one week

questions.explanation: She says she can deactivate the old card so nobody else can use meal plan or building access.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B because the dining hall is where he last had the card—not her first action.

questions.narrator_text: How long will the replacement usually take if he has photo ID?

options.C: Until the lost-and-found returns the old card
options.D: One week after paying by cash only

questions.explanation: With another photo ID, they can print a new card today in about twenty minutes; fee is ten dollars.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—no multi-day wait is stated for this case.

questions.narrator_text: What happens to the student's campus shuttle access?

options.A: It stops until he pays an extra shuttle fee
options.B: It moves to the new card only after 24 hours
options.C: It stays active because it is linked to his student account
options.D: It is canceled when the old card is deactivated

questions.explanation: She says the shuttle is linked to the student account, not the physical card number, so it stays active.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing D because deactivation sounds total—door access and meals move; shuttle does not.
